title: The Island of the Day Before: skeletal ontogeny of the extinct Noronha dwarf-lizard Lygodactylus neglectus Ceríaco & Passos, 2023 (Squamata: Gekkonidae)
content:
Abstract
The study provides a detailed description of the skeletal ontogeny of the extinct dwarf gecko Lygodactylus neglectus, endemic to the oceanic archipelago of Fernando de Noronha, using high-resolution micro-computed tomography of an embryo, a neonate, and adult individuals of both sexes. The main differences among ontogenetic stages involve the degree of ossification, bone fusion, and proportional remodeling, rather than the appearance of novel structures, indicating strong developmental constraints in a miniaturized gekkonid. This work documents for the first time for the genus a complete postcranial skeleton within a comparative ontogenetic framework, including accessory elements such as sesamoids and paraphalanges associated with adhesive locomotion. Subtle sexual dimorphisms in the skull, pelvic girdle, and calcium deposits (endolymphatic sacs) are also characterized and interpreted in part as allometric variation linked to miniaturization and insular reproduction. The authors highlight the importance of historical collections for investigating ontogeny and evolution in rare or potentially extinct insular lineages.
